summary: Discovery/POC scoping call for Cipher Payments. Customer is evaluating Redwood for payment-fraud model serving and interactive agent features. Main decision axes: latency SLO (p90 < 120ms for classification; p95 < 400ms for open-gen chat), cost per 1k requests, data residency and encryption/KMS requirements, and ability to run private deployment for regulated customers. Team favored starting with Hosted for fast iteration then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput; Private deployment required only for specific regulated partners. Agreed to supply workload traces and run a 1-week benchmark comparing Hosted low-latency configs vs Dedicated reserved capacity. Next steps and owners captured.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll give a quick agenda \u2014 scope goals, workloads, success criteria, and then dive into hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
00:00:08 - Liam O'Connor: thanks, yeah quick intro from our side, i'm liam, head of ml at cipher payments, rhea is platform eng, markus security, ana product, ethan sres. we're evaluating vendors for serving our fraud model and a chat-based investigator assistant. timeline is tight, want a pilot in two weeks and a production decision in 8-10 weeks
00:00:28 - Maya Chen: got it, appreciate that. daniel from our infra team will talk technical details after a quick product outline. daniel?
00:00:34 - Daniel Ortiz: hey folks, quick thanks. can you share current stack? are you on k8s, what GPUs, how many QPS, and what's your latency target?
00:00:44 - Rhea Singh: we run kubernetes on GCP, use a mix of nvidia a10g and t4 for internal models. production QPS for fraud classification is about 1,200 reqs/minute at peak, avg 600. For the agent chat it's much lower but latency sensitive. Our SLOs: classification p90 < 120ms, chat p95 < 400ms. Cost pressure is high, want to understand per-token/unit economics
00:01:12 - Daniel Ortiz: okay good. are models open weights or proprietary? do you need KV cache across requests?
00:01:18 - Liam O'Connor: the fraud model is proprietary, smaller (6B-ish), we can share weights to run benchmarks if needed but would prefer not to move them around. The agent uses a 13B open model for now. We do want session state caching for chat and prefix caching for repeated queries, especially for the investigator workflows
00:01:36 - Maya Chen: that maps well to Redwood patterns. quick high level: hosted API gives fastest time-to-value \u2014 you can point traffic our way and start tests immediately, we have auto batching, prefix/kvcache, and low-latency profiles. Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools if you need predictable throughput and isolation; Private gives a VPC/on-prem option for regulated workloads with customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
00:02:00 - Ana Gomez: question \u2014 for private does that mean installing on-prem? we do have a partner bank that requires on-prem only for some data flows
00:02:08 - Daniel Ortiz: private can be VPC-hosted or true on-prem; the on-prem package is heavier (air-gapped, HSM/KMS plumbed). For most customers a VPC private deployment with customer KMS meets bank requirements.
00:02:20 - Markus Weber: our security checklist: SOC2 type II, ISO, SSO via SAML, RBAC, field-level encryption, customer KMS integration, detailed audit logs, ability to disable data retention. can you confirm capabilities?
00:02:35 - Maya Chen: yes we support SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations (Cloud KMS/HSM), audit logs, and configurable retention. we'll share our security pack and SOC2 cert.
00:02:45 - Ethan Park: for the dedicated option, do you support bursting? our traffic is spiky at end of day across timezones
00:02:52 - Daniel Ortiz: yes \u2014 Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity to an extent; it's still capacity-managed so you'd reserve baseline and allow burst to hosted pools if configured. you can set routing policies \u2014 latency-first or cost-first
00:03:05 - Rhea Singh: let's talk numbers. for a POC we want 1-week of realistic traffic replay: 5k requests/day with a mix classifier calls (80%) and chat (20%). We need to see p90/p95 latency, unit cost, and error rates. Also want to test KV cache hit patterns.
00:03:24 - Daniel Ortiz: perfect. For benchmarking we'll need sample prompts, and a small test harness. For hosted we'll run in our low-latency profile; for Dedicated we'll size GPUs \u2014 for your 6B model classification, we likely recommend 2x A10g for baseline throughput with reserved replicas but we need to run real traces to be sure.
00:03:45 - Maya Chen: success criteria \u2014 can you confirm for us what would make this pilot successful?
00:03:50 - Liam O'Connor: success means: 1) classification meets latency SLOs with <0.5% error/regression vs our baseline, 2) cost per 1k requests is below our threshold ($X \u2014 we'll share exact number), 3) security controls pass initial review, 4) operational integration (SRE runbook + metrics ingestion) is validated. If Hosted can meet these then we prefer it for speed. If not, Dedicated and then Private for regulated subsets.
00:04:15 - Maya Chen: good, that aligns with what most customers do. one nuance \u2014 hosted can achieve low latency with smaller models and our low-latency kernels, but if you need strict data residency / KMS with no egress we recommend Private. Dedicated is the middle ground for throughput/cost predictability.
00:04:33 - Ana Gomez: any data exfil risk with hosted? some partners will not allow raw payloads to leave their vpc
00:04:39 - Daniel Ortiz: hosted means processed in our environment; you can enable token redaction and short retention but if absolute isolation is required we'd use Private. For many banks VPC-hosted private meets requirements because logs and data paths stay in their cloud account.
00:04:54 - Liam O'Connor: about model weights \u2014 we prefer bring-your-own-model for the proprietary fraud model. do you support BYOM and how does that change deployment?
00:05:03 - Maya Chen: yes BYOM supported. Hosted BYOM requires us to ingest model artifacts into a secured storage for serving; Dedicated and Private can keep models in your storage via cross-account access or run with customer-provided images. There are different operational notes, we'll document.
00:05:16 - Rhea Singh: are there any limitations on quantization or speed trade-offs? we want best throughput at acceptable quality
00:05:21 - Daniel Ortiz: our runtime supports int8 and mixed quantization paths; sometimes int8 affects some model outputs slightly. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload, and we can include quality regressions in the benchmark plan
00:05:34 - Markus Weber: can we run drift/regression checks as part of POC? we want to compare outputs vs our baseline for false positive/negative rates
00:05:40 - Daniel Ortiz: yes, we'll include evaluation harness to run batch evals and compute model delta metrics. We can also hook in your eval datasets and produce per-prompt diffs and significance stats
00:05:50 - Maya Chen: operational questions \u2014 metrics, tracing, and cost breakdowns?
00:05:54 - Ethan Park: we need per-request latency, token counts, per-model cost breakdown, and traces into our datadog or prometheus
00:06:02 - Daniel Ortiz: we export traces and metrics via otel; per-route token cost and latency breakdowns are available in the Console and via our metrics API. We'll include sample dashboards in the handoff
00:06:12 - Liam O'Connor: pricing \u2014 can you ballpark hosted vs dedicated cost? even rough numbers help us decide pilot scope
00:06:18 - Maya Chen: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet but high level: hosted is usage-based \u2014 good for variable loads and faster ramp; Dedicated is reserved monthly commit which lowers per-token unit costs for high volume. We'll include a sample costing for your projected traffic in the follow-up
00:06:32 - Ana Gomez: timeline \u2014 can we get pilot live in two weeks?
00:06:35 - Daniel Ortiz: two weeks is tight but doable if we get artifacts today: sample prompts, model access or container, and traffic traces. Hosted path is fastest; Dedicated requires reservation lead time for GPUs but we can often spin an initial reserved pool in 1\u20132 weeks depending on region
00:06:52 - Maya Chen: ok plan: Cipher shares artifacts by Friday (2026-03-06). Redwood to return pricing, Dedicated sizing, and benchmark plan by 2026-03-06. We'll schedule a benchmark run week of 2026-03-09 and a technical deep dive with your infra/security the week of 2026-03-09 or 16.
00:07:10 - Rhea Singh: one more Q \u2014 for burst fallback you mentioned routing to hosted pools, is that automatic? does it preserve data residency?
00:07:18 - Daniel Ortiz: fallback policy can be configured; if you route to hosted pool you must accept the hosted data handling. If data residency prohibits that, then we'd only burst within Dedicated or Private pools \u2014 which may limit burst headroom. We'll show policy examples
00:07:33 - Liam O'Connor: sounds good. any major red flags?
00:07:36 - Maya Chen: nothing major, just need the artifacts and we'll run the checks. security pack will answer most compliance questions.
00:07:42 - Markus Weber: please include details on KMS integration options and HSM/bring-your-key flow in the security pack
00:07:48 - Maya Chen: will do.
00:07:50 - Ana Gomez: ok let's recap and next steps
00:07:52 - Maya Chen: recap: 1) Cipher to send prompts, traffic traces, sample model or container creds 2) Redwood to send pricing, Dedicated sizing, security pack, and benchmark plan 3) run 1-week benchmark hosted vs dedicated with telemetry 4) follow-up technical deep dive with security and infra. Owners and dates in action items.
00:08:12 - Liam O'Connor: thanks everyone, we're keen to move quickly.
00:08:16 - Maya Chen: great \u2014 we'll follow up in email and set up the benchmark slot. thanks all
00:08:20 - [call ends]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-transcribed product names (e.g., "k v cache" as "k v cash"), speaker overlaps, and timestamps are approximate. This transcript is verbatim-style and retains filler words and interruptions as recorded.
